technical_and_design_decisions: Build on Spring Boot 3 / Spring Framework 6 with Java 17 baseline, consistent with the referenced platform requirements.

U1: Implement file-based security using Spring Security with user credentials and roles loaded from an externalized configuration/properties file into an in-memory UserDetailsService; all REST endpoints (localhost:9393) are secured via a SecurityFilterChain requiring authentication.

U2: Implement LDAP authentication using Spring Security LDAP with externalized properties (URL, base DN, user/group search filters); integration tests use an embedded LDAP server (e.g., UnboundID) with a test LDIF file.

U3: Implement role-based access control with exactly two roles, Admin (full read/write/manage) and Viewer (read-only), enforced through Spring Security authorization rules applied per endpoint category; roles are assignable in both file-based and LDAP modes.

U4: Extend the existing HDFS sink with Kerberos support using Hadoop's UserGroupInformation with keytab/principal configuration and automatic ticket re-login from keytab; Kerberos settings exposed as sink configuration properties.

U5: Execute as a time-boxed spike only (no production code): evaluate Apache Sqoop, Debezium (CDC), Apache NiFi, and DataX as mass-ingestion options, hold design collaboration sessions, and produce a design specification document with a recommendation.

U6: Implement the HBase sink as a Spring Cloud Stream module using the HBase Java client, with configurable table, column family, and row-key mapping; tested against an HBase mini-cluster/Testcontainers.

U7: Implement the File Roll sink as a Spring Cloud Stream module writing events to rolling files on the local filesystem with configurable directory, filename pattern, and roll-over policy (size/time based).

U8: Implement the JMX source as a Spring Cloud Stream module using Spring Integration JMX support (notification-listening channel adapter) to subscribe to MBean notifications and publish them as messages.
Package each new module with Spring Boot autoconfiguration and configuration metadata, and cover each story with unit tests, integration tests, and user-facing documentation.
assumptions: An existing Spring Cloud Data Flow-like platform already exists exposing REST endpoints at http://localhost:9393/, including an existing (non-Kerberized) HDFS sink and an established stream source/sink module programming model to follow.
A single developer performs all work; estimates are effort in work-hours, not elapsed calendar time, and assume focused work on one activity at a time.
U5 is scoped strictly as a spike: deliverables are research findings and a documented design specification, with no production implementation included in this increment.

Test infrastructure is available or can be embedded: embedded LDAP server, Hadoop MiniKDC for Kerberos testing, HBase mini-cluster or Testcontainers, and a local filesystem for File Roll tests; no procurement or environment provisioning effort is required beyond test configuration.
Access to a real Kerberized Hadoop cluster and a production LDAP server is available for final validation, requiring no additional development effort.
Only Admin and Viewer roles are required; no fine-grained or custom role model is in scope.
Security configuration is file/properties-driven (no UI changes required for U1-U3).

Estimates include unit tests, integration tests, and documentation for each story, plus increment-level integration testing, packaging, and code review rework; they exclude project management overhead and post-release support.
CI/build infrastructure already exists and only needs incremental updates for the new modules.

activities.activity_description: Analyze all eight user stories, define the overall security architecture (U1-U3) and module design conventions (U4, U6-U8), and plan the spike (U5).
Implement Spring Security configuration with users/roles loaded from an external properties file into an in-memory UserDetailsService, securing all endpoints at localhost:9393.
Unit and integration tests verifying authentication success/failure and endpoint protection for file-based users.
Document file-based security configuration properties and usage examples.
Implement LDAP authentication via Spring Security LDAP with externalized connection and search configuration, securing all endpoints.
Unit and integration tests using an embedded LDAP server and test LDIF data to verify authentication against endpoints.
Document LDAP configuration properties, sample setups, and troubleshooting guidance.
Define Admin and Viewer roles and implement authorization rules across all endpoints, integrated with both file-based and LDAP authentication modes.

activities.activity_name: U3: Tests for role-based access control
activities.activity_description: Tests verifying Admin full access, Viewer read-only access, and denial of unauthorized operations per endpoint.
Document the role model, default access rules, and how to assign roles in each security mode.
Add Kerberos support to the HDFS sink: principal/keytab configuration, UserGroupInformation login, ticket renewal, and secure write path.

activities.activity_name: U4: Tests for Kerberized HDFS sink
activities.activity_description: Integration tests using MiniKDC and a Kerberized mini HDFS cluster, covering authentication, renewal, and secure writes.

activities.activity_name: U4: Documentation for Kerberized HDFS sink
activities.activity_description: Document Kerberos prerequisites, keytab/principal setup, and sink configuration options.

activities.activity_name: U5: Spike - research mass-ingestion integration options
activities.activity_description: Investigate alternatives to the JDBC-driver-based jdbchdfs approach (e.g., Apache Sqoop, Debezium/CDC, Apache NiFi, DataX) and compare against requirements.
Facilitate and participate in collaborative design sessions to converge on a mass-ingestion design.
Write the outcome design specification document, including options analysis, chosen design, and follow-up recommendations.
Implement a Spring Cloud Stream HBase sink with configurable table, column family, and row-key mapping for random realtime read/write access to Big Data.
Unit tests and integration tests against an HBase mini-cluster/Testcontainers covering writes, mapping, and error handling.
Document HBase sink configuration properties and usage examples.

activities.activity_name: U7: Implement File Roll sink module
activities.activity_description: Implement a Spring Cloud Stream sink that stores events in rolling files on the local filesystem with configurable directory, naming, and roll-over policies.

activities.activity_name: U7: Tests for File Roll sink
activities.activity_description: Unit and integration tests covering event persistence, file rolling behavior, and configuration validation.

activities.activity_name: U7: Documentation for File Roll sink
activities.activity_description: Document File Roll sink configuration properties and operational notes.
Implement a Spring Cloud Stream source using Spring Integration JMX notification support to subscribe to MBean notifications and publish them as messages.
Unit and integration tests with test MBeans emitting notifications, verifying publish/subscribe behavior end to end.
Document JMX source configuration (MBean selection, notification filters) and usage examples.
End-to-end verification of secured endpoints with both security modes and role enforcement, and stream pipelines using the new HDFS (Kerberized), HBase, File Roll sinks and JMX source.
Add new modules to the build/CI, produce artifacts and configuration metadata, and prepare the increment release.
Perform self-review, address review findings across all stories, and incorporate fixes and refactorings.
